newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA ASTRA BLAMES LOSS ON NEW PRODUCT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA ASTRA BLAMES LOSS ON NEW PRODUCT.

text.p: Romanian listed state railway carriage maker Astra-Vagoane SA blamed a first half loss of 9.67 billion lei on heavy investment on new product development, raw materials, energy, and interest payments.
"We spent heavily on adjusting to a new high-speed wagon which we build under French licence," Astra general manager George Albu told Reuters from the Transylvanian town of Arad.
The licence for the new wagon, which meets international safety and comfort standards, comes from French engineering group De Dietrich .

Astra is contracted by the Romanian SNCFR railway authority to build 200 wagons by the year 2000, with an initial 20 this year and 50 in 1997. The price of the new wagon is approximately $1.4 million.
The deal is part funded by a $42 million loan from France's Societe Generale , guaranteed by the Romanian state.
The new product also left Astra with a 10.24 billion lei loss in 1995, reversing a 1994 profit of 314.11 million.
Astra manufactured the first of the 200 carriages in June and said the new product would ensure growth.
"We have started to feel recovery is ahead thanks to the high-speed wagon," Albu said.
Completition of the first high-speed carriage also helped Astra's bourse price. On Tuesday its stock closed at 5,000 lei, more than double its end-June price of 2,450.
Albu was confident the freight car production line would also boost recovery prospects. Hundreds of such cars have already been exported to Germany, Italy, the Netherlands or neighbouring Hungary.
"We think we'll end 1996 with a turnover of some 100 billion lei," he said.

Romania is embarked on a major rehabilitation of its rolling stock and extensive rail network. It hopes to get up to $420 million in World Bank and European Bank for Reconstruction and Development financing. ($=3,161 lei) -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
